reasoning: This workflow handles lottery winner notifications for FairTix, an event ticketing platform focused on fair access ("tickets for fans, not bots"). When a lottery winner is selected and added to a Google Sheet, it sends them a congratulations email and updates the sheet with delivery status. The email template reveals a 24-hour purchase window and transparent pricing model. The workflow includes error handling that updates the sheet with either success (200) or failure (500) status codes. This is part of their anti-scalping system where tickets are distributed via lottery rather than first-come-first-served.
name: FairTix Lottery Winner Notification
businessNarrative: This workflow notifies customers who won the ticket lottery for high-demand events, giving them exclusive access to purchase within 24 hours. It's a critical component of FairTix's core value proposition - ensuring real fans get tickets instead of bots or scalpers. The transparent pricing model (no hidden fees) and fair queue system reveals a customer-focused ticketing platform competing on trust and fairness rather than just speed.
trigger: New lottery winner added to Google Sheets tracking spreadsheet
dataFlow: Lottery winner data (name, email, event, price) enters from Google Sheets, personalized congratulations email is sent via Gmail, and the sheet is updated with delivery status (200/500) and timestamp

impact.reasoning: Directly enables revenue by notifying winners who can then purchase tickets. Failure means lost sales and damaged trust in the 'fair' lottery system. Time-sensitive with 24-hour purchase window.
impact.failureScenario: Lottery winners don't get notified, miss their 24-hour purchase window, tickets go unsold, customers lose trust in the fairness promise, potential social media backlash about broken lottery system
impact.revenueConnection: Direct - each notification enables a ticket sale within 24 hours

detectability.reasoning: Workflow updates Google Sheets with status codes, but only when it runs. With polling trigger and inactive status, failures would only be noticed by checking the sheet or customer complaints.
detectability.evidence: Status codes (200/500) written to sheet provide audit trail, but no active alerting visible

timeSavingsEstimate: 5-10 minutes per winner (manual email composition and tracking), potentially 50-500 winners per high-demand event

technicalEvidence.errorHandling: Gmail node has onError: continueErrorOutput, branches to either success (200) or error (500) sheet update. No retry logic visible.
technicalEvidence.complexity: 4 nodes, simple linear flow with error branching, clean implementation
